outcome: The end-to-end organization survives adversarial crash, race, duplicate-recovery and stale-currentness scenarios by reconstructing from durable canonical authority, fencing stale capability, reusing the same semantic attempt where required, and remediating only the affected downstream product state without a global recovery scheduler or whole-organization reset.
currentProblem: Integration B provides bounded execution recovery and C through G now have accepted implementation plans for semantic lineage, autonomous activation, exact deployment/QA, and product closure, but there is no single adversarial proof that these local recovery/currentness guarantees compose across crash windows and concurrent supersession without duplicate effects, stale acceptance, hidden central sequencing, or global reruns.
constraints: Recovery authority stays with the boundary owning the affected authority/currentness subject; no central recovery scheduler chooses work or roles.
Durable canonical refs/CAS heads are recovery truth; process memory, queues, hints and conversation state are not authority.
Recovering an in-flight semantic attempt reuses its immutable ExecutionAttemptBinding; repair cannot silently mint a new semantic attempt.
Stale claim/release/input/release-head/QA/projection subjects cannot authorize new effects or current acceptance.
Committed authoritative publication is reused/idempotently reconciled after continuation loss, not duplicated.
Invalidation/remediation is reverse-dependent and bounded; unrelated work remains current.
Historical evidence is immutable; currentness changes through new canonical transitions/revalidation.
Tests may pause production boundaries but cannot add stronger serialization than production.
Fresh-process recovery reconstructs from durable state without conversation context.
Forbidden fallback: whole-organization reset, rerun-all-roles, rebuild-all-artifacts, or manual global recovery order.
successCriteria: Crash after domain output/before publication: fresh recovery reuses the same semantic attempt/binding and publishes at most once.
Crash after publication/before continuation: restart reuses the publication, continues downstream at most once, and does not rerun accepted work.
After claim-generation takeover, the old worker cannot dispatch or publish with stale claim/release authority.
Semantic input drift during execution blocks stale publication, invalidates only reverse dependents, and leaves an unrelated sibling current.
Deployment drift during QA blocks current QualityAcceptance from the old snapshot while preserving historical QA evidence.
Closure racing upstream supersession never leaves stale closure current: closure either commits first then becomes historical, or aborts as stale.
Duplicate recovery workers converge on one logical attempt/publication/continuation with no duplicate semantic output.
Recover/repair of an existing semantic attempt cannot create a second semantic attempt; only new authorized work/input may.
Authority ahead of ProductHistoryHead yields RECOVERY_REQUIRED/NOT_READY until deterministic history/projection reconciliation.
Recovery stays local across the matrix: no global reset/rerun/manual ordering, and unaffected actionable work continues.
